name: Question 20
worked_solution:
First, we let $f(x)={x}^{2}-2x+2.$

Next, we solve $f(x)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+2 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-2\cdot 1\cdot x+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+2 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}-1+2 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2}+1 & =0 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =-1 \\ (x-1)^{2} & ={\text{i}}^{2} \\ x-1 & =\pm \text{i} \\ x & =1\pm \text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots ${x}_{1}=1+\text{i}$ and ${x}_{2}=1-\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression ${x}^{2}-2x+2$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-2x+2 & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2}) \\  & =(x-(1+\text{i}))(x-(1-\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$
